transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
I'm here because I need help dealing with the people who are monitoring me. They have been following me everywhere and trying to ruin my life, and I need it to stop.
That sounds like a very stressful and exhausting experience to go through. How has your mood been lately—have you been feeling particularly down, or perhaps unusually energetic?

My mood has been mostly okay, just really stressed and tired from dealing with all of this constant monitoring. I wouldn't say I feel depressed or unusually energetic, just exhausted from trying to stay safe.
I can understand how carrying that constant stress would be exhausting. Besides noticing these people, have you heard any voices or seen things that other people don't seem to notice?
No, I don't hear voices or see things that aren't actually there. It's just the real, physical people who are constantly following and watching me that I'm dealing with.

It sounds incredibly draining to live with that level of constant vigilance. How has this stress impacted your ability to keep up with your daily routine, like work, hobbies, or taking care of yourself?

Despite how exhausting it is to always be on guard, I am still managing to go to work and handle my daily responsibilities. My routine isn't falling apart, and I can still take care of myself, but the worry is always there in the background. It just takes a lot of effort to keep everything running normally while dealing with this.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports persistent persecutory beliefs of being monitored and followed, but denies auditory or visual hallucinations, disorganized speech, or negative symptoms. Furthermore, their occupational and daily functioning remains largely preserved, which strongly aligns with Delusional Disorder rather than Schizophrenia. Therefore, Schizophrenia has been removed, leaving Delusional Disorder as the final diagnosis.
